name: OPA128 (Burr-Brown Difet electrometer-grade op-amp, TO-99 metal can)
tagline: Burr-Brown's TO-99 Difet electrometer amp (75 fA max bias). Chinese DIYers collect OPA128SM cans for preamps and praise its resolution despite its 1 MHz GBW.
technology: Single-channel Difet (dielectrically isolated FET-input) electrometer-grade op-amp in a TO-99 metal can. The best grade has 75 fA max bias current, 500 uV max offset and 5 uV/C max drift. It is slow, at about 1 MHz GBW and 3 V/us. Marketed as an improved pin-for-pin replacement for the ADI AD515.

part_numbers.notes: Base part number. Graded JM/KM/LM/SM, all in the TO-99 metal can. The exact per-grade limits were not confirmed in this pass.
Lowest commercial grade (per-grade Ib/Vos limits unconfirmed).

Military-temperature grade. CN sellers trade military-pulled cans marked 'OPA128SM/883'. A separate /883B ordering code was not confirmed.

lineage.notes: Datasheet PDS-653, last Burr-Brown printing rev E dated May 1995. Positioned as an improved pin-for-pin replacement for the AD515.
Re-issued the datasheet as SBOS148. The parts went NRND and were discontinued, with DigiKey showing an LTB of 2020-05-14 for OPA128JM.
The OPA128 datasheet names itself an improved pin-for-pin replacement for the AD515.
The OPA129 is a related Difet electrometer amp in SO-8. A TI E2E thread covers its differences from the OPA128.

reputation.summary: Its audio praise is niche and mostly Chinese. On a CSDN listening ranking of classic audio op-amps, 'OPA128SM x2' sits just below the OPA1612 and is credited with good overtone rendering and high resolution. CN DIYers collect military-pulled OPA128SM/883 gold cans as '发烧运放' (audiophile op-amps) for preamps, sometimes selling them alongside the OPA627. The same sources warn that its low GBW and slew rate make it a poor general-purpose audio op-amp, though some value it for DAC I/V stages. It was designed as an electrometer (fA-level input) amplifier, not an audio part.
typical_uses: preamp line stage in CN DIY builds (with a TO-99 adapter)
DAC I/V conversion (per CN forum claims)
design intent: electrometer, photodiode / ionization-chamber / charge amplifiers
caveats: Only 1 MHz GBW and 3 V/us slew, so it is not a general-purpose audio op-amp.
Single channel in TO-99, so dual-socket audio use needs two cans and an adapter.
Discontinued (TI LTB 2020), so most available stock is pulled or surplus.
The praise comes from a small number of Chinese enthusiast sources.

revision_history.changes: This is the last Burr-Brown printing found. The letter E implies earlier revisions A-D, but those were not located and the change content is not documented.
TI assigned a literature number to the Burr-Brown document. It appears to carry the PDS-653E (May 1995) content unchanged.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA128-specific counterfeit report was found. The part has been discontinued since the 2020 lifetime buy, and stock circulating in CN markets is described as military-pulled 'OPA128SM/883' cans, so treat any 'new' stock with suspicion. Remarking of TO-99 Difet parts is plausible. A genuine part's fA-level bias current can only be confirmed with an electrometer-grade test setup. Checking supply current, GBW and slew against the datasheet is a quicker sanity check.
alternatives: OPA627 / OPA637 (Burr-Brown Difet TO-99 for actual audio duty)
open_questions: Dates and content of the earlier Burr-Brown PDS-653 revisions A-D.

No same-part-number silicon change is known. The Difet die appears unchanged through the TI era, but this is unconfirmed.

corrections: Channels changed from 0 to 1 for all part numbers (single op-amp).
Statuses changed from 'unknown' to NRND/discontinued/obsolete. DigiKey shows an LTB of 2020-05-14 for OPA128JM and lists OPA128SM as obsolete.
Added TI literature number SBOS148 and Burr-Brown document PDS-653E (May 1995).
Added the confirmed headline specs: 75 fA max Ib, 500 uV Vos, 5 uV/C drift, 110 dB Aol, 90 dB CMRR, 1 MHz GBW, 3 V/us slew.
Added the AD515 pin-for-pin replacement lineage and the OPA129 sibling.
claims_confirmed: The OPA128 datasheet has TI literature number SBOS148 (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=83971, https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/56727/BURR-BROWN/OPA128.html).
The datasheet copy is Burr-Brown PDS-653E, dated May 1995 (https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/opa128-445402.pdf).

Headline specs are 75 fA max bias, 500 uV max offset, 5 uV/C max drift, 110 dB min Aol and 90 dB min CMRR. It is an improved pin-for-pin replacement for the AD515 (https://www.alldatasheet.com/html-pdf/56727/BURR-BROWN/OPA128/500/1/OPA128.html).
GBW is 1 MHz and slew rate is 3 V/us (https://edg.uchicago.edu/~tang/SNFactory/opa128.pdf).
OPA128JM reached end of life with an LTB of 05-14-2020 (https://www.digikey.com/product-detail/en/texas-instruments/OPA128JM/OPA128JM-ND/301117).

OPA128SM is obsolete, and the variants are listed NRND/discontinued (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/OPA128SM/301120, https://octopart.com/opa128sm-texas+instruments-420293).
The OPA129 is a related part, discussed against the OPA128 on TI E2E (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/712204/opa129-differences-from-opa128).
